lessons.title: 1. Array Sum & Length
lessons.description: In Java, arrays have fixed size and a `.length` field. Implement `findSum(int[] numbers)`.
learning_objectives: Iterate over Java primitive array elements

tests.name: test_find_sum
tests.test_code: int[] arr = {10, 20, 30}; if (Solution.findSum(arr) != 60) throw new AssertionError("Expected 60");

source.name: Oracle Java Tutorials — Arrays — 'The length of an array is established when the array is created'

lessons.title: 2. Finding Min & Max
lessons.description: Find maximum value in a non-empty array.

tests.name: test_find_max
tests.test_code: int[] arr = {3, 9, 2, 8}; if (Solution.findMax(arr) != 9) throw new AssertionError("Expected 9");

lessons.title: 3. Temperature Sensor Analysis (Concept Challenge)
lessons.description: Calculate average reading and count values above threshold.
learning_objectives: Perform statistical array operations in Java

tests.name: test_readings
tests.test_code: double[] r = {22.5, 28.0, 19.1, 31.2}; if (Solution.countAboveThreshold(r, 25.0) != 2) throw new AssertionError("Expected 2");

lessons.title: 4. Array Reversal (Practice)
lessons.description: Implement reverse(int[] numbers) so it reverses the array in place — swap elements from both ends while the left index stays below the right index. The test expects {1, 2, 3, 4} to become {4, 3, 2, 1}.

tests.name: test_reverse
tests.test_code: int[] arr = {1, 2, 3, 4}; Solution.reverse(arr); if (arr[0] != 4 || arr[3] != 1) throw new AssertionError("Expected reversed array");

source.name: Oracle Java Tutorials — Arrays — indexing with brackets
source.license: Oracle Free Use Terms and Conditions (documentation)

lessons.title: 5. Unit 4 Checkpoint: Arrays Mastery
lessons.description: Implement contains(int[] numbers, int target): walk the array (a for-each loop fits nicely) and return true only when target appears. The test expects contains({5, 10, 15}, 10) == true and contains({5, 10, 15}, 99) == false.

tests.name: test_contains
tests.test_code: int[] arr = {5, 10, 15}; if (!Solution.contains(arr, 10)) throw new AssertionError("Expected contains 10"); if (Solution.contains(arr, 99)) throw new AssertionError("Expected not contains 99");

source.name: Oracle Java Tutorials — Arrays — the enhanced for statement
